context: The table lists the tree’s fixed parent–child relationships. The left-hand 7 is the left child of root 1. The right-hand 7 is the right child of node 3.
Traverse the entire tree in preorder (root → left → right) to find paths from root 1 to every node with value 7.

The state list path holds the active path from the root to the current node. The result list res holds a copy of the path for each match. The figure shows path and res using node values. The code stores node objects and makes list copies with list(path). The two 7s are distinct objects.
description: When trying a node, append it to path on entry. If its value is 7, add a copy of path to res. Before leaving the node, pop it from the end of path to restore the path from before this choice.

frames.announcement: Enter root 1 and append 1 to path.
frames.explanation: Start at root 1 and append it to path. Its value is 1, so it does not match 7. Now path = [1] and res = []. Both subtrees remain to be explored. Visit the left-hand 7 next.
frames.key_state: Enter root 1. Now path = [1] and res = [].
frames.title: Enter root 1

frames.announcement: Visit the left-hand 7 and save the path copy [1, 7] in res.
frames.explanation: From root 1, enter the left-hand 7 and append it. This is a match, so save a copy of the path in res. Now path = [1, 7] and res = [[1, 7]]. Continue to its children 4 and 5.
frames.key_state: At the left-hand 7, path = [1, 7]. After saving a copy, res = [[1, 7]].
frames.title: Find the left-hand 7 and save the path

frames.announcement: Enter the left leaf 4, updating path to [1, 7, 4].
frames.explanation: Enter leaf 4, the left child of the left-hand 7, and append it to path. It does not match 7. Now path = [1, 7, 4] and res = [[1, 7]]. Node 5 and the root’s right subtree remain to be explored.
frames.key_state: Enter leaf 4. Now path = [1, 7, 4] and res = [[1, 7]].
frames.title: Enter node 4

frames.announcement: Backtrack from leaf 4 and pop it, restoring path to [1, 7].
frames.explanation: Both empty subtrees of leaf 4 have returned. Pop 4 from path and return to its parent, the left-hand 7. Now path = [1, 7] and res = [[1, 7]]. Node 4 is complete. Explore right child 5 next.
frames.key_state: Pop 4 and return to the left-hand 7. Now path is back to [1, 7] and res = [[1, 7]].
frames.title: Leave 4 and return to the left-hand 7

frames.announcement: Enter the right leaf 5, updating path to [1, 7, 5].
frames.explanation: Enter leaf 5, the right child of the left-hand 7, and append it to path. Its sibling 4 has already been popped. Now path = [1, 7, 5] and res = [[1, 7]]. All nodes in the left subtree have been visited. The root’s right subtree remains.
frames.key_state: Enter leaf 5. Now path = [1, 7, 5] and res = [[1, 7]].
frames.title: Enter node 5

frames.announcement: Leave 5 and then the left-hand 7, restoring path to [1].
frames.explanation: After visiting 5, pop it and return to the left-hand 7. Both its subtrees are complete, so pop that 7 and return to root 1. This frame combines both backtracking steps. Now path = [1] and res = [[1, 7]]. Explore the root’s right child 3 next.
frames.key_state: Pop 5 and then the left-hand 7 to return to root 1. Now path is back to [1] and res remains [[1, 7]].
frames.title: Leave 5 and the left-hand 7

frames.announcement: Enter the root’s right child 3, updating path to [1, 3].
frames.explanation: Enter the right child of root 1, node 3, and append it to path. It does not match 7. Now path = [1, 3] and res = [[1, 7]]. Continue to 3’s left leaf 6 and right leaf 7.
frames.key_state: Enter right child 3. Now path = [1, 3] and res = [[1, 7]].
frames.title: Enter node 3

frames.announcement: Enter the left leaf 6, updating path to [1, 3, 6].
frames.explanation: Enter leaf 6, the left child of 3, and append it to path. It does not match 7. Now path = [1, 3, 6] and res = [[1, 7]]. Only the right child of 3, node 7, remains unvisited.
frames.key_state: Enter leaf 6. Now path = [1, 3, 6] and res = [[1, 7]].
frames.title: Enter node 6

frames.announcement: Backtrack from leaf 6 and pop it, restoring path to [1, 3].
frames.explanation: The visit to leaf 6 is complete. Pop 6 from path and return to parent 3. Now path = [1, 3] and res = [[1, 7]]. Explore the right-hand 7 next.
frames.key_state: Pop 6 and return to node 3. Now path is back to [1, 3] and res = [[1, 7]].
frames.title: Leave 6 and return to 3

frames.announcement: Visit the right-hand 7 and save the second path copy, [1, 3, 7], in res.
frames.explanation: Enter leaf 7, the right child of 3, and append it. This is the second match, so save a copy of the path in res. Now path = [1, 3, 7] and res = [[1, 7], [1, 3, 7]]. All nodes have been visited. Only the final backtracking steps remain.
frames.key_state: At the right-hand 7, path = [1, 3, 7]. After saving a copy, res = [[1, 7], [1, 3, 7]].
frames.title: Find the right-hand 7 and save the path

frames.announcement: Leave the right-hand 7, node 3, and root 1 in order. The path is empty and the search is complete.
frames.explanation: After visiting the right-hand 7, pop it, its parent 3, and root 1 from path in order. This frame combines the final three backtracking steps. The search ends with path = [] and res = [[1, 7], [1, 3, 7]]. Both saved copies remain intact.
frames.key_state: Popping the right-hand 7, node 3, and root 1 completes the final three backtracking steps. Now path = [] and res = [[1, 7], [1, 3, 7]].
frames.title: Leave the right-hand 7, node 3, and root 1

result: Each match in res is an independent list copy. Popping nodes during backtracking changes only the active path, leaving saved solutions intact.
summary: Append each node to path on entry and pop it on exit. Save a copy of the path on each of the two visits to a 7. The search ends with path empty.
